item.content:encoded: Hey Star Trek! Happy Birthday! - Krebs Gorlon. In this video, two of the ugliest men on Earth sit down to discuss a TV show that is now 60 years old! What more could you possibly want from a YouTube? But in all seriousness Rich and Mark finally go in depth into the very first season of Star Trek! They don’t really have a top 5 episodes, because (according to them) they like all the episodes in some way, kind of how you like something about all of your ugly children. They both pick five or so episodes to discuss or highlight or whatever. Rach and Mooboo love to talk about Star Trek so they doed. They make the time to sit down and talk for nearly three hours. Mark peed in his pants and the dumb one pooped in his diaper. The dumb one is the guy wearing the Scottish hat and the fat, ugly one is the guy that “edits” these videos. I mean, if I were to look up the definition of “editing” I don’t think It would read: “Leaves everything in” but hey, what else are these guys gonna do with little time they have left? They’re literally weeks away from the grave talking about how a 60 year old show was a good show. My god, is this what they are choosing to do with their remaining days??!? Young people today don’t even watch TV or Movies! They don’t have the patience. They watch hip-flips on their switch kicks and play Rubblox on their hyperinterlinked cerebrum-chips. Getting someone under 45 to watch an episode of Star Trek is like getting an old in the grocery store to move to one side of the aisle while walking in slow motion searching for salve. Life has become a nightmare from which I can’t escape. An endless series of holidays and birthdays that all culminate in an endless series of hospital visits and funerals. In the middle of all that we eat, we sleep, and we watch TV. So in this 2 hour long video about Star Trek Mark and Ronaldo first discuss a few off topic topics. Mainly the current state of Star Trek. We are in the middle of the streaming of season 4 of Strange New Worlds (With a short season 5 yet to come) and one more season of Starfleet Academy (Viewership predicted to be less than 100) After that who can truly say what is next for a once beloved franchise that looks like a beaten up grandma. I guess them two guys are writing a movie where Star Trek is going to be some kind of spy action thriller and they are bringing back Khan. Oh boy! Can't wait for that. I hate this world and I hate the people that are in charge of entertainment today. A bunch of fart clowns I say it. FART CLOWNS. The dumbest people on earth are in charge. They say you can never go home again. But with old TV shows you can. You can put on an old show or movie and watch it and say, "Ah, this is nice. This doesn't hurt me so deeply" As Mark and Raunch's bodies begin to rot from the inside and their vision begins to blur. As their farts begin to slip out as they lose anal elasticity, they can always sit back and watch and talk about old Star Trek. These two men are made of ash, moments before a strong wind blows through. So enjoy things while they last because you never know when a dimwit is gonna roll into town with a circus of low talent scum TV writers and 58 producers and ruin your whole life.

item.title: ROBIN SWICORD - Writer / Director
item.content:encoded: SEASON 2 - EPISODE 209 Robin Swicord - Writer / DirectorIn this episode of the Team Deakins Podcast, we speak with writer and director Robin Swicord (WAKEFIELD, WHEN THEY SEE US, PRACTICAL MAGIC). Throughout the episode, Robin is frank about her experience working in the film industry as a woman, and we discuss how she's seen the culture and behaviour within the industry change over the years. Robin wrote the script for the 1994 adaptation of LITTLE WOMEN, and she shares what it took for the studio to finally greenlight the film after 12 years of development. She also reflects on the long development process of BENJAMIN BUTTON, and she reveals what her initial vision for the story was. After years as a writer, Robin was able to direct her first feature, THE JANE AUSTEN BOOK CLUB, and she shares how she cast the film on short notice and how she prepped for it as a first-time director. We later discuss how she shot her second film as a director, WAKEFIELD, in just 18 days, and she reflects on what she brought from her experiences on her first film to the second one.This episode is sponsored by Aputure ⁠

item.title: JOHN LEE HANCOCK - Writer / Director
item.content:encoded: SEASON 2 - EPISODE 208 John Lee Hancock - Writer / DirectorIn this episode of the Team Deakins Podcast, we speak with writer and director John Lee Hancock (THE HIGHWAYMEN, THE ROOKIE, A PERFECT WORLD). John was born and raised in Texas and we learn how he made the transition from practicing law to screenwriting and what he stayed busy with to survive in Los Angeles after moving there. John later reflects on learning filmmaking from Clint Eastwood and Kevin Costner during the production of A PERFECT WORLD (which John wrote), and he reveals how he came up with the idea of the film. We also learn how producer Mark Johnson (Season 2, Episode 97) accidentally set him up to direct his first film, and John reveals some of the benefits of being a writer while also working as a director. John also reflects on the grand-scaled production of THE ALAMO, and we discuss the historical and cultural backdrop of Texas at the time of the events of the movie. Towards the end, John shares some information with us about his next film, and we discuss the economic difficulties of filming within the United States that lead to productions shooting abroad. Recommended Viewing: A PERFECT WORLD

item.title: When Hollywood Stopped Trusting Directors - Heaven's Gate
item.author: FilmStack
item.content:encoded:
It’s June 1980, and director Michael Cimino is finally showing United Artists the first cut of Heaven’s Gate.
By then, the western was already a disaster. It was nearly four times over budget, almost a year late, and had one of the most notorious productions in Hollywood history. But maybe it was all worth it.
Before the screening started, Cimino warned them the final version might be fifteen minutes shorter.
Then they sat there for five hours and twenty-five minutes, watching a film that would ;be torn apart by critics, would humiliate United Artists, and change how Hollywood looked at directors.
This is the story of when Hollywood stopped trusting directors. This is Heaven’s Gate.

Our special guest this week is Johnny Flynn, who stars in & Sons—A dysfunctional family drama with a twist. His character Richard is one of three long suffering sons to Billy Nighy’s A.N. Dyer, a mega-successful novelist turned alcoholic recluse and personal disaster zone. Johnny chats to Simon about the movie, its unusual filmmaking process, and working alongside Nighy, Imelda Staunton, George McKay and Noah Jupe as part of its all-star ensemble cast. Plus we hear a little about his upcoming performances as Paul Simon in South-African-set drama The Road Home, as a beleaguered sheriff in western A Prayer For The Dying, as Dostoevsky in The Idiots, and as Lucuis Malfoy (i.e. Jason Isaacs) in Harry Potter. I do wish someone would give this lad a bit of work, he must be desperate for something to get his teeth into…
Mark reviews & Sons, as well as two more of the week’s most exciting titles. First up, Coyote vs Acme, a live action animation hybrid that sees Looney Tunes’ murderous canine Wile E. item.title: JOHN CARROLL LYNCH - Actor / Director
item.content:encoded: SEASON 2 - EPISODE 207 John Carroll Lynch - Actor / DirectorIn this episode of the Team Deakins Podcast, we speak with actor and director John Carroll Lynch (BALLARD, LUCKY, FARGO). During our conversation, John tells us what originally drew him into acting, and we discuss an actor's function and place in film, television, and the theatre. As an actor, John has been directed by filmmakers ranging from Clint Eastwood to David Fincher to Ethan and Joel Coen (Season 1, Episode 33), and we discuss how he adapts to different methods of working. We later spend much of the episode discussing John's directorial debut, LUCKY, and we learn how he came to direct the film, how he worked with actor Harry Dean Stanton to develop a script based on his own life, and what it was about the film that attracted him to join in the first place. John also reflects on his experience directing the late David Lynch in the film, and we ask him what to expect in his next movie as a director. We worked with John on FARGO, and it was great catching up with him.Recommended Viewing: LUCKY
